docs.title: The contribs
docs.text:
js-contrib is organised like fastjet-contrib: each contrib lives in its own folder under contribs/ and is switched on separately.

Contrib What it is Build Extra dependencies Docs on this site PyJetscape pybind11 bindings (pyjetscape_core), the jetscape Python package with the Pythonic layer, Python modules, the PyFNOHydro trampoline, the production drivers and examples C++ (-DUSE_JS_PYJETSCAPE=ON); already built in the container and the Mac wheel pybind11; h5py, hdf5plugin, pyyaml; PyTorch optional ([fno]) Python, Run FnoHydro Fourier-neural-operator hydrodynamics as a C++ module through LibTorch, plus the bulk ROOT I/O library C++ (-DUSE_JS_FNO_HYDRO=ON) libtorch (~2 GB), ROOT Live PyTorch FNO hydro FastHydro MC-Glauber initial state and a fast 3+1D Milne finite-volume hydro solver, with the MATTER + LBT → CausalLiquefier jet-deposition workflow and paired background/jet evolutions pure Python, reuses PyJetscape PyTorch, scipy, h5py, pyyaml FastHydro Visualization 3D PyVista rendering of the hydro evolution, resampled from Milne to Cartesian coordinates, with a jet parton-shower overlay pure Python, reuses PyJetscape pyvista, scipy, vtk, imageio (imageio-ffmpeg for .mp4) 3D visualization

FastHydro and Visualization have no CMake build of their own. They read the framework through the PyJetscape bindings and so need a current pyjetscape_core.

docs.title: The pieces of a working setup
docs.text:
Component Repository / image Role X-SCAPE JETSCAPE/X-SCAPE, branch contrib the framework and the C++ physics modules (MATTER, LBT, liquefier, hadronization, …) MUSIC4GPU jhputschke/MUSIC4GPU, branch XSCAPE MUSIC viscous hydro with CUDA and Metal back ends iSS jhputschke/iSS, branch smash_ready Cooper–Frye particlization (oversampling, SMASH-ready output) 3D MC-Glauber jhputschke/3dMCGlauber, branch cap_hard_quark_draws the initial state LBT tables JETSCAPE/LBT-tables LBT's scattering tables (fetched by get_lbtTab.sh, or xscape-fetch-data lbt with the wheel) js-contrib jhputschke/js-contrib this package: bindings, drivers, productions, tools, analysis Production images jhputschke/xscape-prod everything above, built, for Linux with NVIDIA GPUs (amd64 and arm64) Development images jhputschke/xscape-fno4d-dev the build environment without sources, for a source build on Linux with NVIDIA GPUs Mac wheel jhputschke/xscape-macos everything above, built for Apple Silicon with Metal, installed with uv FNO models Zenodo record 16647726 the trained FNO hydro models and their training data (Live PyTorch FNO hydro)

The X-SCAPE scripts external_packages/get_*.sh clone MUSIC4GPU, iSS and 3D MC-Glauber at pinned commits. When you update X-SCAPE, run them again so the pins take effect. See Source build.

docs.title: Versions that belong together
docs.text:
js-contrib X-SCAPE MUSIC4GPU Mac wheel main contrib (head) XSCAPE (pinned by get_music4gpu.sh) v0.1.0

The container images and the Mac wheel are built from one consistent set of commits, so there is nothing to match by hand. With a source build, keep js-contrib main together with X-SCAPE contrib.

docs.title: Building this site
docs.text: The site is built with MkDocs and the Material theme. Its pages are the Markdown files in website/, and its configuration, including the navigation, is in mkdocs.yml at the repository root. The docs/ folder (design notes, plans, benchmarks) is not part of the site.

docs.title: Preview locally
docs.text:
python3 -m venv ~/.venvs/js_docs
~/.venvs/js_docs/bin/pip install -r website/requirements.txt
~/.venvs/js_docs/bin/mkdocs serve          # from the repository root

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000. The page reloads whenever you save a file. To build the static site into _site/ and stop on any broken link or anchor:

~/.venvs/js_docs/bin/mkdocs build --strict

docs.title: Change a page
docs.text:
• Edit the Markdown file in website/. Each page also has an edit button that opens the file on GitHub.
  • A new page also needs an entry under nav: in mkdocs.yml.
  • Link to other pages with relative .md paths (../run/osdf.md). Link to files in the repository with full GitHub URLs (https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib/blob/main/...), because those files are not part of the site.
  • Available features include admonitions (!!! note), content tabs (=== "Docker"), Mermaid diagrams, and math (\( … \)). See the Material reference.

docs.title: Publish
docs.text:
Building the site does not publish anything. One way to put it on GitHub Pages at https://jhputschke.github.io/js-contrib/ is:

~/.venvs/js_docs/bin/mkdocs gh-deploy      # builds and pushes to the gh-pages branch

Then, in the repository's Settings → Pages, set the source to the gh-pages branch.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: The utils/ folder holds the tools around the simulations. They help you plan a production, watch it run, check its files, and move them. Each one is a plain script, and --help lists all of its options.

docs.title: Planning: prodwizard.py
docs.text:
You choose a production preset and a machine. The wizard writes the launch command with the settings measured on that machine. It estimates events per hour, duration, disk and memory (each marked measured or estimated) and checks the plan. It never starts jobs.

python utils/prodwizard.py --list                                  # presets and machines
python utils/prodwizard.py --preset auau_jet --machine 2x3090 --events 2000
python utils/prodwizard.py --preset oo_hadrons --machine slurm_a100 --events 10000 --save launch_oo.sh
python utils/prodwizard_tui.py                                     # the same as an interactive wizard (Textual)
Presets Machines auau_jet, auau_particlize_only, auau_hadrons_only, oo_hadrons, oo_full, pbpb_zjet 2x3090, gb10, m3max, slurm_v100, slurm_a40, slurm_a100, slurm_l40s

docs.title: Launching
docs.text:
Script What it does run_jobs.sh (in each production folder) runs a campaign of jobs with unique seeds, several at a time on one GPU; see the productions launch_2gpu.sh, launch_2gpu_oo.sh one Docker container per GPU on a two-GPU machine, a disk guard, and optional upload to the OSDF while it runs slurm_prod_array.sh stage 1 (hydro + jets) as a SLURM array in the production container, one GPU per task; PROD=oo for O+O slurm_hadronize.sh stage 2 (hadronization) as a SLURM array on a CPU partition

See Clusters, GPUs and monitoring for how they fit together.

docs.title: Monitoring: jobmon.py
docs.text:
jobmon.py watches a running (or finished) campaign using only what the jobs already write (logs and .json). It reports jobs done, running and failed, events per hour, ETA, disk per event, the machine's GPUs and memory, and the most frequent warnings. It also flags failed jobs with their last log lines.

python utils/jobmon.py out/                 # one summary; exit code 1 if a job failed or is flagged
python utils/jobmon.py out/ --watch         # live view, refreshed every 10 s
python utils/jobmon.py out/ --tui           # terminal UI: sortable job table, live log, problems tab

check_deposition.py flags Au+Au jet jobs whose deposited droplets per event fall below half the campaign's median. This is a rare failure that leaves no log message.

docs.title: Inspecting files: h5_inspect.py
docs.text:
h5_inspect.py lists every group and dataset of an HDF5 file with its shape, dtype, storage and attributes. For the js-contrib hydro formats it also summarises the grid, the axes, the freeze-out, the shower/, source/ and diag/ tables, and flags inconsistencies. It needs only h5py and numpy.

python utils/h5_inspect.py out/AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001.h5           # summary + tree
python utils/h5_inspect.py FILE.h5 --stats [--event 0]              # per-feature min/max/mean, NaN/inf
python utils/h5_inspect.py FILE.h5 --attr prod_user_xml             # one attribute in full

docs.title: Moving files: OSDF and Google Cloud Storage
docs.text:
Script What it does remote_transfer/js_osdf.py ls, du, download and upload for the Pelican namespace osdf:///fno4hic (reading is public; writing needs a token) remote_transfer/js_gcs.py the same commands for a Google Cloud Storage bucket upload_follow.py uploads a campaign's finished jobs to the OSDF while it runs, and can delete the verified uploads locally

Both transfer scripts select files by kind (--what pair|h5|root|all), skip files that are already there, and check every transfer by size and CRC32C. Each one builds its own Python environment on first use. See Data on the OSDF.

docs.title: Environments and builds
docs.text: Tool What it does analysis_env/setup_analysis_env.sh, check_env.py the analysis venv, and a check that opens every file of a production (Analysis environment) conda_install/ creates and checks the js_fno conda environment (Source build) configure.sh interactive CMake configurator for X-SCAPE + js-contrib (needs dialog) gen_pyjetscape_stubs.py regenerates the .pyi type stubs of pyjetscape_core for editors Dockerfile.dev, Dockerfile.prod the development and production images (BuildContainerProd.md, BuildContainerDev.md)

docs.title: Running the productions
docs.text: A production is a set of ready-made scripts that run one physics setup of X-SCAPE many times and write the results as HDF5 files for analysis and for training the ML hydro surrogates. This section shows how to run them: a first event, the two-stage Au+Au jet production, O+O with initial-state radiation, Z+jet and other collision systems, and how to scale up to clusters with many GPUs and share the outputs on the OSDF. You need one of the two ready-made setups, the production container (Linux with an NVIDIA GPU, or an HPC cluster) or the xscape wheel (Apple Silicon Mac), or a source build.

docs.title: The productions
docs.text:
All productions live in contribs/PyJetscape/example/, each in a folder with a driver script, a user XML in example/config/, and a run_jobs.sh for campaigns. In the container they are under /opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example; on a Mac xscape-examples copies them into a directory of yours.

production physics writes page prod_AuAu_0_10 0–10 % Au+Au at 200 GeV: 3D MC-Glauber strings, MUSIC on the GPU, no jet hydro evolutions on a chosen output grid, in the FNO4d training format (run_prod.py) below prod_AuAu_0_10_jet the same medium with a jet: PythiaGun, Matter + LBT, the causal liquefier feeding the energy lost back into a second MUSIC run a background/jet pair of hydro evolutions per event, the freeze-out surfaces and final partons, and (in stage 2) the hadron files Au+Au jets prod_OO_isr O+O at 200 GeV with initial-state radiation (PythiaIsrGun + iMATTER), one MUSIC run per event, Matter + LBT, iColored jet hadronization the hydro evolution, the jet hadrons, the bulk hadrons (in the job or later) O+O with ISR Z+jet (utils/zjet/) Pb+Pb at 5.02 TeV, 0–30 %, with a Z → ee/μμ trigger, through the jet production's driver hadron files with the Z and its leptons recorded per event Z+jet and other systems your own system e.g. Pb+Pb at the LHC: a copy of the jet XML with the collision changed as prod_AuAu_0_10_jet Z+jet and other systems

The Pythonic example pythonic/oo_workflow.py runs the O+O chain in about 140 lines of Python and is the quickest way to see the whole chain work: Your first event.

docs.title: The general shape
docs.text:
Every production works the same way.

  • A driver and a user XML. The driver (run_prod_jet.py, run_prod_oo_isr.py, run_prod.py) runs one job: one seed, N events, one set of output files. The physics is in the user XML; the driver takes it (or yours, with --user-xml), fills in the job (events, seed, the hard process and its pT̂ windows, what to store), checks it, and writes the XML it ran next to the output (<stem>.xml) and into the files.
  • run_jobs.sh for campaigns. It runs many jobs, -j P at a time on one GPU, each in its own working directory, and is resumable: run the same command again and finished jobs are skipped.
./run_jobs.sh [-j P] [--mps] [--stagger S] [--campaign NAME] NJOBS EVENTS_PER_JOB FIRST_SEED [OUTDIR] [driver options]
  • Seeds. FIRST_SEED 0 gives every job a new seed drawn from OS entropy and checked against the seed registry seeds_used.tsv next to OUTDIR, so two campaigns never share a collision. FIRST_SEED > 0 gives exactly those seeds, for reproducing a file or comparing settings on the same events. The seed that ran is stored in every file, and --seed <it> reproduces the file bit for bit.
  • Stages. The expensive part, hydro and jets, runs on a GPU. Hadronization, which needs only the stored freeze-out surfaces and final partons, runs later on CPUs, as often as wanted. Productions with little oversampling can make the hadrons in the GPU job instead and skip the second stage.
flowchart LR
    X["user XML<br/>+ driver options"] --> S1
    subgraph S1 ["Stage 1: GPU"]
        R["run_jobs.sh<br/>→ driver, one job per seed"]
    end
    S1 --> P["stem.h5<br/>hydro (pair)"]
    S1 --> Q["stem_particlize.h5<br/>surfaces + partons"]
    S1 -.->|"--hadrons-only,<br/>O+O --bulk-hadrons"| H
    Q --> S2
    subgraph S2 ["Stage 2: CPU"]
        Z["run_hadronize.py<br/>→ hadronize.py"]
    end
    S2 --> H["stem_hadrons_*.h5<br/>hadron files"]
    P --> F["FNO training,<br/>hydro analysis"]
    H --> A["analysis venv,<br/>ROOT export"]
    P & Q & H -.-> O[("OSDF<br/>osdf:///fno4hic")]

Why two stages. Hydro needs a GPU; sampling hadrons from a freeze-out surface (iSS) and fragmenting partons (Pythia) does not, and it is cheap per sample. Storing the surfaces, with their full viscous information, lets you choose the number of oversamples, the hadron selection and the precision after the expensive part is done, on any CPU nodes, without rerunning the hydro. The result is the same as hadronizing in the job, checked bit for bit.

docs.title: Hydro only (prod_AuAu_0_10)
docs.text:
The simplest production writes 0–10 % Au+Au hydro evolutions (no jet) straight to FNO4d training HDF5 on an output grid chosen in a YAML file (default example/config/grid_fno.yaml). It is the training-data production for the FNO surrogates and uses the same run_jobs.sh as the others:

cd prod_AuAu_0_10                                # in your copy of the examples
python run_prod.py --events 10 --seed 1          # -> out/AuAu_0_10_seed0001.h5
python run_prod.py --events 1 --seed 1 --grid my_grid.yaml --dry-run   # check a grid
./run_jobs.sh --campaign mb_a 20 25 0            # 20 jobs x 25 events, unique seeds

Each job writes <stem>.h5 (the evolutions), .xml, .json and, through run_jobs.sh, .log. Full options: the folder's README. What the files hold: What a production writes.

docs.title: What a job writes
docs.text:
file written by content <stem>.h5 stage 1 the hydro evolution (Au+Au jet: the background and jet-leg pair) on the output grid <stem>_particlize.h5 stage 1 (--write-particlize; O+O by default) the freeze-out surfaces, the final partons and the shower initiators: the input to hadronization <stem>_hadrons_{bulk_jet,bulk_bg,jet_frag}.h5 stage 2, or the job itself the hadrons: iSS on the jet-leg surface (bulk + wake), on the background, and the fragmented jet partons <stem>.xml, .json, .log stage 1 the job XML as run, a summary (seed, events, cross sections, checks), the log

The stem is AuAu_0_10_jet_seedNNNN for an explicit seed and AuAu_0_10_jet_<campaign>_NNNN (job number) in a FIRST_SEED 0 campaign; O+O files start with OO_isr_. The formats are described in What a production writes.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Your first event: one O+O event through the whole chain, then two Au+Au jet events.
  • Au+Au jets (two stages): the main production, from the first job to a campaign.
  • Clusters, GPUs and monitoring: SLURM, several GPUs, jobmon.py.
  • Data on the OSDF: download existing productions or share yours.

docs.title: Au+Au jets in two stages
docs.text: prod_AuAu_0_10_jet is the main production: 0–10 % Au+Au collisions at 200 GeV (3D MC-Glauber strings, MUSIC on the GPU) with a hard jet whose energy loss feeds back into the medium. Each event is written as a pair of hydro evolutions, the background and the same event with the jet, and, for hadron-level work, as the freeze-out surfaces and partons that a second stage turns into hadrons on CPUs. Use it for the medium response to jets (the wake) in hydro and in hadrons, for jet observables with a realistic background, and as training data for the ML hydro surrogates. This page goes from a single job to a campaign; the first two events are in Your first event.

docs.title: How an event is made
docs.text:
IS (3dMCGlauber) -> Hard (PythiaGun) -> NullPreDynamics
   -> MUSIC_1                    background leg               -> arr_bg
   -> Liquefier + Eloss          Matter + LBT on MUSIC_1's medium -> droplets
   -> MUSIC_2                    the same strings + the droplets  -> arr

Why pairs. Both legs start from the same initial condition and are bit-identical until the first droplet deposits, so arr - arr_bg is the jet's effect on the medium and nothing else: no event-by-event fluctuation of the bulk to subtract statistically. The same holds at hadron level: iSS on the jet leg's surface minus iSS on the background's.

The background leg doesn't depend on the jet. So a background can be shared by several jets (--reuse N, or several pT̂ windows with --pthat-bins): MUSIC_1 runs once per background, MUSIC_2 once per jet. MUSIC_2 also starts from MUSIC_1's saved state just before the first droplet can deposit (τ ≈ 1 fm/c), with bit-identical output; this is on by default. The physics settings (EOS, liquefier, Matter and LBT) are discussed in The physics.

docs.title: 1. Checks before a campaign
docs.text:
The driver run_prod_jet.py runs one job: one seed, N events. Run these from the production folder (in the container: /opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet, Docker's start directory; on a Mac: your xscape-examples copy), with the output under a directory you can write:

# 1. the XML and the grid, checked; the job XML written, no event
python run_prod_jet.py --events 1 --seed 1 --dry-run --outdir out_val

# 2. null test: MUSIC_2 without the liquefier must reproduce the background bit for bit
python run_prod_jet.py --events 1 --seed 901 --write-particlize both --no-deposit --outdir out_val

# 3. validation: the hadrons are also made in the job, to compare with stage 2
python run_prod_jet.py --events 2 --seed 900 --write-particlize both --validate-inline --outdir out_val
  • Null test. arr == arr_bg in every frame (diag/frames_identical == ntau in the pair file), and the two stored surfaces are identical:
python -c "import numpy as np; from jetscape.particlize_h5 import ParticlizeFile as P; \
p = P('out_val/AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0901_particlize.h5'); \
print(np.array_equal(p.surface('jet', 0), p.surface('bg', 0)))"      # True
  • Validation. hadronize.py --use-stored-seeds on the validation file must reproduce the in-job hadrons bit for bit (run it without --keep-bits-* or --eta-max). The script is in Checks before a campaign of the folder's README. --validate-inline changes the jet sample of a seed (it adds tasks, which shifts the energy loss's random streams): use it for validation jobs only.
  • One event with a jet: diag/n_droplets > 0, and the legs differ only after the first deposit.

With pT̂ windows, also run the null test with the windows (--pthat-bins … --no-deposit). For hardware checks (GPU found, settings arrived) see Checking a run.

docs.title: 2. Stage 1: hydro and jets on the GPU
run_jobs.sh
docs.text:
./run_jobs.sh [-j P] [--mps] [--stagger S] [--campaign NAME] NJOBS EVENTS_PER_JOB FIRST_SEED [OUTDIR] [run_prod_jet.py options]
argument NJOBS number of jobs = number of output files; total events = NJOBS × EVENTS_PER_JOB -j P at most P jobs at once (default 1); it doesn't create jobs FIRST_SEED 0: a new seed per job, never repeated (a campaign, the usual choice); > 0: seeds FIRST_SEED, FIRST_SEED+1, … --campaign NAME names the files AuAu_0_10_jet_NAME_0001.h5, …; without it, the start time OUTDIR the output directory: the argument after FIRST_SEED (default ./out), not --outdir. One campaign per OUTDIR after OUTDIR options for every job, e.g. --write-particlize both, --pthat-bins …
  • Restarting: run the same command again. Jobs whose .json says complete are skipped, unfinished ones are redone (in a seed-0 campaign with a new seed). The skip test looks only at file names and event counts: give every setting its own OUTDIR.
  • Seed registry: seeds_used.tsv in OUTDIR's parent, shared by the campaigns side by side there, under a lock.
  • A seed is a set of collisions. The same seed gives the same background in every campaign, whatever the jet settings. That is what paired comparisons want, and wrong for campaigns meant as more statistics: use FIRST_SEED 0 for those.
  • --mps (CUDA only) lets the P jobs share the GPU through CUDA MPS; --stagger S starts the first P jobs S seconds apart. Both are discussed in Clusters.
  • At the end, OUTDIR/run_jobs.finished is written; each job leaves <stem>.log, <stem>.json and <stem>.xml.

docs.title: What to store
docs.text:
option stores use (default) the hydro pair <stem>.h5 FNO training data, hydro-level wake --write-particlize both + <stem>_particlize.h5: both freeze-out surfaces (full viscous information), the final partons, the shower initiators hadron level: jet − background. Add it to every job that should get hadrons later --write-particlize jet + the jet leg's surface only the jet event's hadrons without background subtraction (turns the MUSIC_2 restart off) --write-particlize both --particlize-only only the particlize file, no pair file hadrons without the hydro history: ~2.5× less disk, ~3 s per event faster --hadrons-only only hadron files, made in the job; no stage 2 little or no oversampling (below)

The pair file is unchanged, byte for byte, by --write-particlize.

docs.title: pT̂ windows and shared backgrounds
docs.text:
A background costs about as much as a jet leg. For a real campaign, share each background among several jets in several pT̂ windows:

... --pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --jets-per-bin 5
  • How. One Pythia per window, each with its own seed and cross section; event i uses window i mod K. --reuse is set to K × M (here 3 × 5 = 15), so one background serves 15 events, 5 in each window.
  • EVENTS_PER_JOB must be a multiple of K × M (15, 30, 45, …).
  • Cost. An event costs about (1 + 1/(K·M)) / 2 of an event with its own background: 0.53 for K·M = 15.
  • Cross sections. Each window records its σ; combine windows with those weights (Hadrons). Results stitched over windows have errors correlated through the shared backgrounds; per-window results and jet − background don't.
  • --reuse N alone shares a background among N jets of one window. --pthat-min/--pthat-max set a single window (default 50–70 GeV); --hard pgun --pgun-pt P shoots one parton.

docs.title: The parton rapidity cut
docs.text:
At low pT̂ the jets spread far in rapidity, and much hydro time would go to events that cannot reach a mid-rapidity measurement. --parton-ymax Y keeps only events whose shower-initiating partons pass a rapidity cut; rejected events are regenerated in Pythia before any shower or hydro, and the cross sections are corrected by the kept/tried fraction.

--parton-y-mode keeps the event if for leading (default) the hardest parton has |y| < Y the hardest jet in the acceptance both the two hardest have |y| < Y dijets any either of the two hardest has |y| < Y inclusive jets, the medium response

The cut only selects events; the analysis applies its own. So Y must be looser than the analysis acceptance: --parton-ymax 0.6 (leading) is complete for jets up to |η_jet| ≈ 0.4–0.5; for inclusive R = 0.4 jets at |η_jet| < 0.6 use --parton-ymax 0.7 --parton-y-mode any. For wake hadrons at |η| < η_max, about Y ≈ η_max + 1 with any.

docs.title: Defaults worth knowing
docs.text:
• MUSIC's late time step. From τ = 3 fm/c MUSIC steps 0.05 fm/c instead of 0.02. The stored frames stay at 0.1 fm/c; the medium changes at 1e-3 and the hadron level by less than ±2 %. Keep one setting per campaign: --late-dtau 0 gives a constant step.
  • MUSIC_2 from MUSIC_1's state. Bit-identical output, ~25 core-s less per jet event; --no-music2-restart turns it off. Every job log says restart at the start, on or off.
  • EOS 91 (hotQCD with the SMASH hadron list), which iSS decays itself; --eos 9 only to rerun older campaigns.
  • The output grid of the pair file is example/config/grid_fno.yaml (64 × 64 × 32 cells, x, y ±12.2 fm, η_s ±4.84); --grid FILE for another. Never mix grids in one training set.

Every option of run_prod_jet.py: the Options table of the folder's README.

docs.title: 3. Stage 2: hadronization on CPUs
docs.text:
hadronize.py turns one particlize file into hadrons: iSS samples both stored surfaces (with viscous corrections), Pythia fragments the stored partons. It needs no GPU and no MUSIC. run_hadronize.py runs it over a whole campaign, -j P files at a time, and skips files whose hadrons are complete:

DockerApptainerMac / source build 
IMG=jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126          # the image of stage 1
docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 \
  -v "$HOME/prod:/work" $IMG \
  ./run_hadronize.py /work/AuAu_a -j 8 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50

PROD=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
apptainer exec --env OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 --pwd "$PROD" --bind "$SCRATCH/prod:/work" \
  xscape_prod.sif ./run_hadronize.py /work/AuAu_a -j 8 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50

python run_hadronize.py out_had -j 8 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50

Inputs are directories, particlize files or quoted globs. Per production file it writes <stem>_hadrons_bulk_jet.h5, <stem>_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5 and <stem>_hadrons_jet_frag.h5 next to it.

option -j P processes at once, ~1.4–1.7 GB and one core each --oversample N iSS samples per jet-leg surface (default 100) --n-frag K Pythia fragmentations of the partons per event --oversample-bg auto a background shared by N events gets N × the samples: the optimal split for jet − background under --reuse --oversample-bg per-pthat-bin for --pthat-bins campaigns analysed per window: M × the samples (M = --jets-per-bin) --correlated correlated jet/background sampling: jet − background ~8× less noisy at |η| < 1 for the same samples (not together with --oversample-bg) --keep-bits-p B, --keep-bits-x B round momenta and positions to B mantissa bits: 12 and 8 store 58 % of the bytes with no visible effect on ensemble observables --eta-max X, --charged, --no-x store only |η| < X (2: ~60 % of the bytes), charged hadrons, no positions --tags a subset of bulk_jet,bulk_bg,jet_frag --follow keep running next to a stage 1 that is still writing; stop when its campaign is finished --dry-run show the plan only --force redo complete files (e.g. with other settings)

Decide the hadron settings once per campaign

The precision (--keep-bits-*), the selection (--eta-max, --charged, --no-x) and the background oversampling must be the same for every file: pass the same flags to every call, --follow and restarts included. Complete files are skipped whatever settings made them. Nothing is lost for good: the particlize file and the stored seeds reproduce the exact hadrons with --force. Keep the validation job at full precision and without cuts.

Alongside production. Start run_hadronize.py --follow next to run_jobs.sh; it hadronizes each file as its job completes and stops when the campaign writes run_jobs.finished. On a machine whose cores are the limit, its cores come out of stage 1's rate, so on clusters stage 2 usually runs separately on CPU nodes (SLURM). Only the particlize files need to travel there: they are self-contained.

docs.title: Hadrons in the job (--hadrons-only)
docs.text:
For campaigns with little or no oversampling (1–10 samples per jet event), the hadrons can be made in the GPU job itself: run_prod_jet.py --hadrons-only writes only the three hadron files, the undecayed bulk hadrons (*_primary.h5, for SMASH later; --keep-primaries 0 turns them off) and the .json. No pair or particlize file, no stage 2:

./run_jobs.sh -j 8 --mps 60 45 0 /work/AuAu_ho --reuse 4 --hadrons-only

Its options are hadronize.py's (--oversample, default 1; --n-frag, default 1; --correlated; --eta-max, --charged, --no-x; the rounding is --hadron-keep-bits-p/-x). The hadrons equal those of the two-stage path for the same seed, bit for bit. What is lost: no surfaces (no new samples later) and no hydro history. On the GB10 it cost ~4 % in events/h against --particlize-only and wrote 0.64 MB per event, against ~160 MB in two stages.

docs.title: 4. A realistic campaign
docs.text:
The campaign setting used for the production runs: three pT̂ windows, 5 jets per window per background, the leading parton at |y| < 0.6, everything stored for hadronization.

DockerApptainerMac 
IMG=jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126          # for a campaign: a dated tag or the digest
mkdir -p ~/prod/lbt_cache
docker run -d --name c1 --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=3 -e OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive -e MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block \
  -e LBT_TABLE_CACHE=/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin -v "$HOME/prod:/work" $IMG \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 6 --mps --stagger 12 --campaign pth10-40_eta06_c1 67 15 0 \
    /work/AuAu_0_10_pth10-40_eta06_c1 \
    --pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both
docker logs -f c1             # progress;  docker stop c1 stops it cleanly

-j 6 with 3 threads each suits one GPU with ~24 cores and 64 GB; size -j to your machine (~2–3 cores and ~7 GB per job).

PROD=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
mkdir -p $SCRATCH/prod/lbt_cache
apptainer exec --nv \
  --env OMP_NUM_THREADS=3,OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive,MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block \
  --env LBT_TABLE_CACHE=/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin \
  --pwd "$PROD" --bind "$SCRATCH/prod:/work" xscape_prod.sif \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 6 --stagger 12 --campaign pth10-40_eta06_c1 67 15 0 \
    /work/AuAu_0_10_pth10-40_eta06_c1 \
    --pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both

On a SLURM cluster use the array script instead: Clusters.

cd ~/xscape/examples/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
OMP_NUM_THREADS=5 OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive KMP_BLOCKTIME=0 \
  caffeinate -i ./run_jobs.sh -j 3 --campaign pth10-40_eta06_c1 67 15 0 ~/xscape/prod/AuAu_c1 \
    --pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both

On a Mac, split the cores between the jobs (-j × threads ≈ the performance cores) and use passive, or several jobs gain nothing; --mps is CUDA only. caffeinate -i keeps the Mac awake.

That is 67 jobs × 15 events = 1,005 events on 67 backgrounds. Then stage 2, with the background sampled per window and the hadrons rounded:

./run_hadronize.py /work/AuAu_0_10_pth10-40_eta06_c1 -j 16 \
  --oversample 400 --oversample-bg per-pthat-bin --n-frag 50 --keep-bits-p 12 --keep-bits-x 8

400 samples per jet event, 5 × 400 = 2,000 per background and window, 50 fragmentations.

What to expect. Measured with the campaign setting:

2 × RTX 3090 (24 cores), 10 jobs per GPU 2,160 events/h (1,080 per GPU), ~25 s per event in a loaded job GB10, -j 4 --mps (earlier code) 336 events/h host memory per job ~6–7 GB with the shared LBT tables; plan 7 GB (5 GB with --particlize-only) disk, stage 1 0.243 GB per event (pair + particlize); 0.097 GB with --particlize-only stage 2 ~340 events/h per core at 500 oversamples (10.6 s per event, both legs; 8.8 s with --correlated): ~6–7 cores keep up with 2,000 events/h disk, hadrons ~100 MB per leg and event at 500 oversamples, full precision; 58 % of that with --keep-bits-p 12 --keep-bits-x 8, and ~60 % of that again with --eta-max 2

On a cluster, the sizing per GPU type and a 12,000-event SLURM example are in Clusters, GPUs and monitoring; the hardware numbers in GPU acceleration.

Pin the image, one per campaign

The moving tags (cu126) change with every build, and different builds can differ in the last digits or more. For a campaign use a dated tag (cu126-<YYYYMMDD>-<commit>) or the digest, the same one on every machine, and note it: the files don't record which image made them. Run the whole campaign on GPUs: MUSIC's CPU path differs systematically (~0.2 % in multiplicity).

docs.title: After the campaign
docs.text:
• Watch and check it: utils/jobmon.py OUTDIR --watch, and the deposition check utils/check_deposition.py OUTDIR, which flags the rare job whose jets deposited far less than the rest: Clusters, GPUs and monitoring.
  • Move the files: --what h5 (particlize + hadron files) for the analysis, --what pair for FNO training: Data on the OSDF.
  • Analyse: Hadrons (HadronFileReader, cross-section weights, jet − background), Jets with FastJet, ROOT and C++ (run_h5toROOT.py).

Full details, every option and the measurements: prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/README.md and docs/README_2stage.md.

docs.title: Clusters, GPUs and monitoring
docs.text: A production job keeps a GPU only partly busy: much of an event is host work (string deposition, Matter and LBT, the freeze-out search, writing). So a GPU needs several jobs at once, and the cores and host memory per GPU, not the GPU, usually set the rate. This page covers running at scale with the production container: the launch settings, SLURM arrays with Apptainer, several GPUs in one machine, watching a campaign with jobmon.py, and what to do when a run goes wrong. The single-machine commands are on the production pages (Au+Au jets, O+O).

docs.title: Sizing: jobs, cores, memory
docs.text:
For the Au+Au jet production with the current code, per job:

host memory plan 7 GB per job (5 GB with --particlize-only), plus ~8 GB per node; Pb+Pb ~16 GB cores ~1 core busy on average, with OpenMP bursts: 2–3 threads per job GPU memory ~1 GB per job: a 16 GB V100 holds 8–10 jobs disk 0.243 GB per event with pair + particlize files

An O+O job needs ~1.5 GB and, with 10 oversamples in the job, ~6 core-s per event. So set the number of jobs per GPU from the cores and memory a GPU gets: about cores / 2–3, and about (memory − 8 GB) / 7 GB. Lower the number of jobs where a node gives a GPU less, not the threads per job below 2. The measured and extrapolated rates per GPU type (V100, A40, A100, L40S, RTX 3090, GB10, M3 Max) are in GPU acceleration.

Before a large campaign, on the first node: a 20–30 min sweep of the jobs per GPU (e.g. 8, 12, 16) at the planned cores. Record events/h by makespan, the GPU use (nvidia-smi dmon -s u) and the memory peak. If the GPU stays below ~75 % busy while the cores are full, more cores per GPU pay, more jobs don't.

docs.title: Launch settings
docs.text:
None of these changes the output; together they decide how many jobs fit and how fast they run.

setting how why jobs per GPU run_jobs.sh -j P the GPU needs several jobs to stay busy (10 on an RTX 3090 with 12 cores per GPU) threads per job OMP_NUM_THREADS ≈ cores per GPU / P, at least 2 more threads than cores oversubscribe them OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive environment idle OpenMP threads sleep instead of spinning MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block environment the host sleeps while it waits for the GPU: ~30 % less CPU per event at the same throughput LBT_TABLE_CACHE=FILE environment; FILE in a bound, writable directory all jobs map one read-only copy of LBT's 0.66 GB of tables: −0.6 GB and 6–11 s of start-up per job. The first job writes it --stagger S run_jobs.sh option the first P jobs start S s apart, so their memory peaks don't coincide (12 for 8–10 jobs per GPU) --mps run_jobs.sh option, CUDA only the jobs share the GPU through CUDA MPS: +5–12 % where it works

CUDA MPS in containers

MPS is not assured inside containers (on the GB10 the daemon does not start in one) and has never been tried on a cluster: run without it first, and test with nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d; echo $? inside the container. Two daemons in one container hang the second GPU's jobs. If the site runs MPS itself (--gres=mps), don't add --mps.

In Docker pass the variables with -e, in Apptainer with --env A=1,B=2. On a Mac the same rule holds without MPS: OMP_NUM_THREADS=5 OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive KMP_BLOCKTIME=0 ./run_jobs.sh -j 3 … on a 16-core M3 Max.

docs.title: SLURM: one GPU per array task
docs.text:
utils/slurm_prod_array.sh runs a campaign as a job array in the production container: each task gets one GPU and runs P jobs on it with the launch settings above. SLURM gives whole GPUs, and only jobs in one allocation can share a GPU, so one SLURM job per production job would leave the GPUs mostly idle.

1. Pull the image once, on a login node (a .sif holds one CPU architecture; on x86 login nodes with arm64 GPU nodes such as GH200, add --arch arm64):

apptainer pull xscape_prod.sif docker://jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126-<date>-<commit>

2. Make the LBT table cache once with one 1-event job (otherwise 20 tasks starting together each write their own copy; add your site's -p/-A):

PROD=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
WORK=$SCRATCH/xscape_prod; mkdir -p $WORK/lbt_cache
srun --gres=gpu:1 --cpus-per-task=4 --mem=16G --time=0:20:00 \
  apptainer exec --nv --env LBT_TABLE_CACHE=/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin \
  --pwd "$PROD" --bind "$WORK:/work" xscape_prod.sif \
  python run_prod_jet.py --events 1 --seed 1 --outdir /work/lbt_cache/init \
    --seed-registry none 2>&1 | grep "LBT:"
rm -r $WORK/lbt_cache/init                 # the test event, not needed

The grep shows LBT: wrote the table cache /work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin. Where arm64 and amd64 nodes share a file system, keep one file per architecture (LBT_CACHE=/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1_arm64.bin).

3. A trial, then the campaign (from a js-contrib checkout):

# trial: 2 tasks, 2 jobs of 15 events each
SIF=$PWD/xscape_prod.sif CAMPAIGN=pth10-40_eta06_c2 NJOBS=2 EVENTS=15 P=2 \
  EXTRA_ARGS="--pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both" \
  sbatch --array=0-1 --time=2:00:00 utils/slurm_prod_array.sh

# the campaign: 20 tasks x 40 jobs x 15 events = 12,000 events on 800 backgrounds
SIF=$PWD/xscape_prod.sif CAMPAIGN=pth10-40_eta06_c2 NJOBS=40 EVENTS=15 \
  EXTRA_ARGS="--pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both" \
  sbatch --array=0-19 utils/slurm_prod_array.sh

The defaults, P=10 jobs per GPU with --gres=gpu:1 --cpus-per-task=20 --mem=96G, are an A100's or A40's share of a node; for other GPUs pass P and the sbatch options (e.g. V100s: P=8 … sbatch --cpus-per-task=16 --mem=64G). The script sets OMP_NUM_THREADS = cpus / P itself (and warns below 2). At the 3090's measured rate, that 12,000-event campaign is ~11 GPU-hours, ~2.9 TB of stage-1 files and ~0.9 TB of hadrons.

variable default SIF $HOME/xscape_prod.sif the image WORK $SCRATCH/xscape_prod bound to /work; writable, shared by the tasks PROD auau oo runs prod_OO_isr CAMPAIGN, NJOBS, EVENTS, P campaign name, jobs per task, events per job, jobs at once per GPU EXTRA_ARGS options for the driver (run_prod_jet.py / run_prod_oo_isr.py) BINDS more binds, e.g. "$PWD/xml:/xml" for your own XML TAG_PREFIX the production's file names, e.g. PbPb_0_30_seed SEED_MODE registry ranges with SEED_BASE: task t runs seeds SEED_BASE + t·NJOBS …, no cross-node lock needed MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC, LBT_CACHE, STAGGER, USE_MPS block, /work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin, 12, 0 the launch settings (LBT_CACHE=none, STAGGER=0 to turn off) CHECK_DEPOSITION 1 after the jobs, flag jobs whose droplets per event fall below half the median
  • Output: WORK/CAMPAIGN/t000/, t001/, … with one shared seed registry WORK/CAMPAIGN/seeds_used.tsv. The script checks that file locks work across nodes, or use SEED_MODE=ranges.
  • Restarting: submit the same command again; each task skips its finished jobs. A task that runs out of time resumes.
  • Time: at ~25 s per event in a loaded job, a 15-event job takes ~6–7 min; allow 2× on V100s. Longer jobs (30 or 45 events) amortise the start-up better.
  • Memory: SLURM counts the page cache of the HDF5 files being written; if tasks are killed near the limit, raise --mem by ~10–15 % rather than lowering P.
  • Disk: one fast GPU can write more than an OSDF upload takes (an L40S up to ~0.7 TB/h with pair files). Use --particlize-only unless the hydro history is needed, and upload_follow.py (Data on the OSDF).
  • O+O: PROD=oo CAMPAIGN=OO_c1 EXTRA_ARGS="--bulk-hadrons 10 --no-particlize --no-hydro-file" sbatch --mem=40G utils/slurm_prod_array.sh.

docs.title: Stage 2 on CPU nodes
docs.text:
utils/slurm_hadronize.sh hadronizes the campaign with the same image, without a GPU: task t runs run_hadronize.py on WORK/CAMPAIGN/t<ttt>/, the directory of stage-1 task t, one process per core.

SIF=$PWD/xscape_prod.sif CAMPAIGN=pth10-40_eta06_c2 \
  HAD_ARGS="--oversample 400 --oversample-bg per-pthat-bin --n-frag 50 --keep-bits-p 12 --keep-bits-x 8" \
  sbatch --array=0-19 utils/slurm_hadronize.sh
  • Defaults: --cpus-per-task=16 --mem=32G; HAD_ARGS defaults to --oversample 400 --n-frag 50 --keep-bits-p 12 --keep-bits-x 8. Keep HAD_ARGS the same for every task and resubmission.
  • PROD=oo hadronizes the O+O bulk (--tags bulk_bg is added); INPUTS="/work/…" takes other inputs (directories, particlize files or quoted globs, as paths inside the container).
  • Memory ~1.6–1.7 GB per process: ask for ~2 GB per core. One process does ~340 Au+Au events/h at 500 oversamples, so ~6–7 cores keep up with 2,000 events/h of stage 1.

docs.title: Several GPUs in one machine
docs.text:
MUSIC always uses the first GPU it sees, and run_jobs.sh doesn't assign GPUs: on a machine with several GPUs, run one campaign per GPU, each with its own CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (or its own container), OUTDIR and campaign name. OUTDIRs side by side share the seed registry.

Ready-made for Docker on two GPUs: utils/launch_2gpu.sh starts one container per GPU, each running run_jobs.sh with MPS, guards the disk and can upload every finished job to the OSDF while the campaign runs. utils/launch_2gpu_oo.sh does the same for O+O. Run them from utils/ of a js-contrib checkout:

cd js-contrib/utils
# Au+Au with the defaults: 10 jobs per GPU, 3 threads, shared LBT tables, staggered start,
# blocking CUDA sync; 60 jobs x 45 events (a multiple of 20 jobs)
IMAGE=jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 \
nohup ./launch_2gpu.sh 60 45 0 /data/camp_pth3 --campaign pth3 \
    --pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 \
    --write-particlize both > /data/camp_pth3.log 2>&1 &

# O+O, hadron files only (defaults: 8 jobs per GPU, 3 threads, MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block, MPS)
nohup ./launch_2gpu_oo.sh 64 100 0 /data/OO_had --campaign had1 \
    --bulk-hadrons 100 --no-particlize --no-hydro-file > /data/OO_had.log 2>&1 &

./launch_2gpu.sh [options] NJOBS EVENTS_PER_JOB [FIRST_SEED] [OUTBASE] [driver / run_jobs.sh options]
  • NJOBS is the total: GPU0 gets the first half, GPU1 the rest. Output goes to OUTBASE/gpu0/ and OUTBASE/gpu1/, with a shared seed registry. With FIRST_SEED 0 both directories hold files of the same names (different seeds): keep the directories.
  • Options before NJOBS: --lbt-cache FILE (Au+Au default /work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin, made first if missing, ~1 min; none turns it off), --stagger S (Au+Au default 12; 0 off), --min-free SIZE (the disk guard: stops both containers below SIZE free, default 50G), and the upload options --upload REMOTE, --delete none|pair|all, --keep-free SIZE, --verify-every N (Data on the OSDF).
  • Environment: IMAGE, JOBS_PER_GPU (default 10; O+O 8), OMP_THREADS (default 3), WORKDIR (mounted as /work, default $HOME/prod_test), MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC (default block), TAG_PREFIX. For an image older than 2026-10-10: JOBS_PER_GPU=8 OMP_THREADS=4 ./launch_2gpu.sh --lbt-cache none --stagger 0 ….
  • Stop with Ctrl-C or kill (both containers and the uploader stop); resume with the same command.

Measured on 2 × RTX 3090 (24 cores, 125 GB) with the campaign setting: 2,160 events/h for Au+Au at 10 jobs per GPU, 105 GB host memory peak; 13,728 events/h for O+O with hadron files only. Details: utils/README_launch.md.

By hand, or with Apptainer (one container for all GPUs, no --mps):

apptainer exec --nv --env OMP_NUM_THREADS=3,OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive,MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block \
  --env LBT_TABLE_CACHE=/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin \
  --pwd "$PROD" --bind "$SCRATCH/prod:/work" xscape_prod.sif bash -c '
  trap "kill \$(jobs -p) 2>/dev/null; wait" INT TERM
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ./run_jobs.sh -j 8 --stagger 12 --campaign AuAu_gpu0 24 45 0 /work/AuAu/gpu0 --write-particlize both &
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 ./run_jobs.sh -j 8 --stagger 12 --campaign AuAu_gpu1 24 45 0 /work/AuAu/gpu1 --write-particlize both &
  wait'

Under SLURM, if CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is already set (e.g. 2,3), use those numbers.

docs.title: Monitoring a campaign
docs.text:
utils/jobmon.py reads what the jobs write (their logs, .json summaries and the run_jobs.* markers) and shows jobs done / running / failed, events, events/h, the ETA, disk per event, the failed jobs with their last log lines, the deposition check, edge hits, skipped events and the most frequent warnings. It works on Docker, SLURM and Mac output alike, during a run or after.

utils/jobmon.py /data/c1                  # OUTBASE: its gpu0/, gpu1/, ... (or t000/, ...) are taken
utils/jobmon.py /data/c1 --njobs 100      # count the jobs not started yet too
utils/jobmon.py /data/c1 --watch          # live view, every 10 s
utils/jobmon.py /data/c1 --tui            # terminal UI: sort, filter, a job's details and live log
utils/jobmon.py /data/c1 --all            # every job; exit code 1 if one failed or is flagged

It needs only the standard library; --watch uses rich if installed and --tui needs textual (both in the analysis environment). For a workshop, the TUI runs in a browser: textual serve "utils/jobmon.py /data/c1 --tui" (package textual-dev).

  • A job counts as running while its driver process is alive (on the machine that runs the jobs, containers included); on another machine, while its log changed in the last 15 min (--stale).
  • The drivers' event … done in lines reach the log in blocks, so event counts jump by ~10–15 at a time; PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 in the jobs' environment avoids it. The s per event are exact.

The deposition check. Once, in ~250 campaign jobs, all events of one job lost almost no jet energy (1–5 droplets per event instead of 13–34), with a correct background and no warning in the log; the same seed alone was normal. Check every campaign for it:

utils/check_deposition.py /work/AuAu_a                     # every job summary below it
utils/check_deposition.py /data/c1/gpu0 /data/c1/gpu1      # one campaign in two directories

It flags a job whose droplets per event fall below half the campaign's median (--fraction) and exits 1 if one is flagged. To redo it, move its files (<stem>.*) out of OUTDIR and run the campaign's command again. slurm_prod_array.sh runs it on each task's directory.

docs.title: Checking a run
docs.text:
In a job log, OUTDIR/<stem>.log:

line means [MUSIC-GPU] CUDA device: <GPU name> (cc X.Y, …) the hydro runs on that GPU [MUSIC-GPU] OMP wait policy: passive (max threads N) the thread settings arrived [MUSIC-GPU] host sync: block MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block arrived LBT: wrote the table cache … / LBT: tables mapped read-only from … the LBT cache works (grep -L "mapped read-only" OUTDIR/*.log lists jobs without it) late step: delta_tau 0.02 -> 0.05 fm/c at step 130 … MUSIC's late time step is on restart MUSIC_2 starts from MUSIC_1's state … / restart OFF: … the MUSIC_2 restart, on or off with the reason … done in … s per event the speed: events/h = jobs × 3600 / s per event No CUDA device found, falling back to CPU no GPU: ~7–10× slower and systematically different (~0.2 %). Don't add that output to a GPU campaign PairH5Writer: event i: the jet leg has e = … on the transverse edge of the output grid fluid above freeze-out reached the stored box's edge (diag/{bg,jet}_hit_edge); a few per campaign are expected, frequent ones mean the grid is too small

Each job also writes <stem>.json (seed, events written, settings, events_hit_edge, droplets_total), and a campaign ends with OUTDIR/run_jobs.finished.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
symptom cause and fix ./run_jobs.sh: No such file (Apptainer) no --pwd "$PROD"; or call $PROD/run_jobs.sh --outdir: give OUTDIR as the argument after FIRST_SEED OUTDIR is the 4th argument of run_jobs.sh, not an option Read-only file system: …/seeds_used.tsv OUTDIR's parent isn't writable: put OUTDIR one level inside a bound directory (/work/out) only one job runs with -j 2 NJOBS is 1: -j only limits how many run at once No CUDA device found / jobs much slower no GPU visible: --nv / --gpus, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, or per-campaign MPS on several GPUs kernel launch … failed: no kernel image is available the image lacks this GPU's architecture (e.g. V100 with a cu130 image): use cu124 or cu126; discard that output --mps: could not start the MPS daemon MPS doesn't work in this container or site: drop --mps jobs killed (OOM) plan ~7 GB per Au+Au job plus ~8 GB per node: lower -j, use LBT_TABLE_CACHE and --stagger, or ask for more --mem busy-spinning threads, the libgomp warning OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive before launching the GPUs stay ~60 % busy whatever -j expected: the cores per GPU set the rate. More cores per GPU help, more jobs don't one job's events have far fewer droplets than the rest the rare failure of the deposition check: redo that job unrecognized arguments: --late-dtau (or --no-music2-restart) an older image without the option: drop it a failed job its OUTDIR/<stem>.log; rerun the same command (finished jobs are skipped)

More cases: docs/README_2stage.md, §7.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Data on the OSDF: move the outputs, or upload them while the campaign runs.
  • What a production writes: the files of a finished campaign.

docs.title: Your first event
docs.text: Before a campaign, run one event through the whole chain and look at what comes out. This page does that twice: first one O+O event at 200 GeV with the Pythonic example oo_workflow.py (3D MC-Glauber, Pythia with initial-state radiation, MUSIC on the GPU, Matter + LBT, iColored and iSS: under a minute), then two Au+Au jet events with the production driver of the two-stage production. You need the production container, the xscape wheel on a Mac, or a source build.

docs.title: 1. One O+O event
docs.text:
oo_workflow.py reads a user XML (default: oo_workflow.xml next to it, made from the O+O production's template), runs the events and writes the bulk and jet hadrons of each event to two hadron files. The examples can't run inside the read-only image or the installed wheel (they write next to themselves), so xscape-examples first copies them into a directory of yours.

DockerApptainerMacSource build 
mkdir -p work
docker run --rm --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/work:/work" -w /work \
  jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 bash -c \
  'xscape-examples /work/examples && cd /work/examples/pythonic &&
   python oo_workflow.py --events 1 --outdir /work/out_oo'

The hadron files land in ./work/out_oo/. --gpus all gives the container the GPU and --user makes the files yours. Other CUDA versions (cu130 for Blackwell and GH200, cu124 for older drivers): Production container.

apptainer pull xscape_prod.sif docker://jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126
W=$SCRATCH/xscape; mkdir -p $W
apptainer exec --bind $W:/work xscape_prod.sif xscape-examples /work/examples
apptainer exec --nv --pwd /work/examples/pythonic --bind $W:/work xscape_prod.sif \
  python oo_workflow.py --events 1 --outdir /work/out_oo

Apptainer needs --nv for the GPU and --pwd for the working directory: it ignores the image's own and starts where you launched it. On a cluster run this on a GPU node (in a batch script, or after salloc).

source ~/.venvs/xscape-0.1.0/bin/activate      # the environment of the installation
xscape-examples ~/xscape/examples
cd ~/xscape/examples/pythonic
python oo_workflow.py --events 1 --outdir ~/xscape/out_oo

MUSIC runs on the Mac's GPU (Metal) without any setting; the event takes under a minute (27 s on an M3 Max). The LBT tables must have been fetched once (xscape-fetch-data lbt, part of the installation).

cd X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/pythonic
python oo_workflow.py --events 1 --outdir out_oo

In the environment PyJetscape was built in, with the jetscape package importable (Source build). The script finds the X-SCAPE tree it sits in and runs the build X-SCAPE/build_gpu, or the one $JETSCAPE_BUILD names (--build DIR overrides both).

The options of oo_workflow.py:

option default --xml FILE oo_workflow.xml the user XML: O+O 200 GeV, b < 3 fm, pT̂ 20–40 GeV, 20 iSS oversamples per event --events N the XML's (3) events --seed S the XML's (7) the framework seed --outdir DIR ./out_oo output directory --name NAME the XML's file name (oo_workflow) the file stem --build DIR $JETSCAPE_BUILD, else $XSCAPE/build_gpu the X-SCAPE build (leave it alone in the container and the wheel) --keep-workdir off keep the job's working directory OUTDIR/work/<name> with the modules' side files

docs.title: What it prints and writes
docs.text:
Between the modules' own log lines (MUSIC, iSS, LBT, Matter), the script prints one line per event and a summary. One event on an M3 Max (source build) gave:

oo_workflow: /…/out_oo/oo_workflow.xml
event 0: 17 final partons, 157350 surface cells, 8361 bulk hadrons, 116 jet hadrons, 15.7 s
oo_workflow: 1 event(s) written, skipped none
  /…/out_oo/oo_workflow_hadrons_jet_frag.h5
  /…/out_oo/oo_workflow_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5

The bulk-hadron count is summed over the event's 20 oversamples. In out_oo/:

file content oo_workflow.xml the job's XML as run, with --events and --seed applied oo_workflow_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5 the bulk: iSS on MUSIC's freeze-out surface, one sample per oversample, with the event record (pT̂, the Glauber numbers, seeds) per unit oo_workflow_hadrons_jet_frag.h5 the jet hadrons of iColoredHadronization, one sample per event, with the partons that started the showers (initiators/)

A module that throws inside an event costs that event only: it is listed as skipped, and the run goes on.

docs.title: A look at the hadrons
docs.text:
The files are in the jetscape.hadrons_h5 format of all productions. In the same environment (or the analysis environment, which needs no X-SCAPE):

import awkward as ak
import jetscape as js

jet = js.HadronArray.from_h5("out_oo/oo_workflow_hadrons_jet_frag.h5")
bulk = js.HadronArray.from_h5("out_oo/oo_workflow_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5")
print(jet, "|", bulk)          # HadronArray(116 hadrons in 1 samples) | HadronArray(8361 hadrons in 20 samples)
print(jet.info["units"]["pthat"])                 # the event record: pT-hat, Glauber numbers, seeds

b = bulk.to_awkward(by_unit=True)                 # events x oversamples x hadrons
ch = b[js.select(b, "charged")]
print(ak.mean(ak.num(ch[abs(ch.eta) < 0.5], axis=2)))   # dN_ch/deta at |eta| < 0.5, averaged over oversamples

The oversamples of one event share one fluid: average over them, they are not independent collisions. The notebook version of the run, pythonic/oo_workflow.ipynb, goes on from here: awkward views, PDG selections, spectra with errors, FastJet on every event and every oversample in one call. The interface is described in The Pythonic interface; the O+O analysis in O+O.

Make it yours

oo_workflow.py is also a template: change the XML (--xml my_job.xml) and the per-event block that decides what is stored. For a production with campaigns, seeds and restarts, use the O+O production itself: O+O with ISR.

docs.title: 2. Two Au+Au jet events
docs.text:
Now the main production's driver, run_prod_jet.py: two 0–10 % Au+Au events at 200 GeV, each a background and a jet leg (two MUSIC runs), with the freeze-out surfaces and the partons stored for hadronization (--write-particlize both). Then stage 2 turns them into hadrons on the CPU.

DockerApptainerMacSource build 
IMG=jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126
mkdir -p prod
# stage 1 (Docker starts in prod_AuAu_0_10_jet)
docker run --rm --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/prod:/work" $IMG \
  python run_prod_jet.py --events 2 --seed 1 --write-particlize both --outdir /work/out
# stage 2: no GPU
docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD/prod:/work" $IMG \
  python run_hadronize.py /work/out -j 4 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50

EX=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example
W=$SCRATCH/xscape; mkdir -p $W
# stage 1
apptainer exec --nv --pwd $EX/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet --bind $W:/work xscape_prod.sif \
  python run_prod_jet.py --events 2 --seed 1 --write-particlize both --outdir /work/out
# stage 2: no GPU, no --nv
apptainer exec --pwd $EX/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet --bind $W:/work xscape_prod.sif \
  python run_hadronize.py /work/out -j 4 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50

cd ~/xscape/examples/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
# stage 1: about 40 s on an M3 Max
python run_prod_jet.py --events 2 --seed 1 --write-particlize both --outdir ~/xscape/prod/out
# stage 2, on the CPU
python run_hadronize.py ~/xscape/prod/out -j 4 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50

cd X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
python run_prod_jet.py --events 2 --seed 1 --write-particlize both --outdir out
python run_hadronize.py out -j 4 --oversample 500 --n-frag 50

Put the output one level inside your directory

Every job records its seed in seeds_used.tsv in the parent of its output directory. So write to /work/out (or ~/xscape/prod/out), not to /work itself, whose parent is inside the read-only image.

With an explicit --seed 1 the stem is AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001. Stage 1 writes AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001.h5 (the hydro pair: the jet leg arr and the background arr_bg), AuAu_0_10_jet_seed0001_particlize.h5 (both freeze-out surfaces and the final partons), the job's .xml and .json. Stage 2 writes next to the particlize file:

file hadrons <stem>_hadrons_bulk_jet.h5 iSS on the jet leg's surface: the bulk with the jet's wake <stem>_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5 iSS on the background's surface <stem>_hadrons_jet_frag.h5 the jet partons, fragmented by Pythia

The difference between the first two is the medium's response to the jet, at hadron level. Read the three together with HadronFileReader: Hadrons.

A first look at the hydro pair

arr - arr_bg is the jet's effect on the medium and nothing else: both legs start from the same initial condition and are bit-identical until the first droplet deposits. With h5py: f["arr"][0] - f["arr_bg"][0] for event 0 (channels energy density, vx, vy, vz). More in Hydro and hadrons together.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Au+Au jets (two stages): from these two events to a campaign.
  • O+O with ISR: the O+O production behind oo_workflow.py.
  • Notebooks: the analysis notebooks to run on these files.

docs.title: O+O with initial-state radiation
docs.text: prod_OO_isr runs O+O collisions at 200 GeV with X-SCAPE's initial-state radiation (ISR) workflow: the hard scattering's incoming partons are showered backward in time by iMATTER, the 3D MC-Glauber strings are made from what the hard scattering left, MUSIC evolves that medium, and Matter + LBT shower the jets through it. The jet hadrons come from iColoredHadronization, which follows the colour flow of the ISR and the beam remnants; the bulk hadrons from iSS. Use it for small-system studies where the hard process and the bulk come from the same nucleon–nucleon collisions: multiplicity and centrality biases of hard-triggered events, flow, jets in a small medium. The tuned O+O 3D MC-Glauber and MUSIC parameters are those of X-SCAPE's O+O example, tuned at 200 GeV.

docs.title: What is different from Au+Au
docs.text:
IS: 3dMCGlauber (O16, positions only)
 -> Hard: PythiaIsrGun at one binary collision
          -> IsrManager / iMATTER       ISR, backward in time
          -> MCGlauberGenString         strings, the hard partons' momentum subtracted
 -> MUSIC                              ONE hydro run per event
 -> Eloss: Matter + LBT in the medium   the final-state shower
 -> JetHadronization: iColored          jet hadrons, in the job
 -> SoftParticlization: iSS             bulk hadrons, in the job or later
  • One MUSIC run per event, no pair. The medium is made from what each event's hard scattering left (its partons' momentum is subtracted from the colliding nucleons), so a medium belongs to one hard event: there is no background leg, no jet − background, no hydro reuse, and no jet deposition into the fluid.
  • Every event is hard-triggered: exactly one hard scattering, at a binary collision drawn uniformly. glauber_ncoll is recorded per event to weight the geometry (O+O analysis). Centrality comes from the impact parameter: the default b < 3 fm is about 0–24 % of the O+O cross section.
  • The jet hadrons are made in the job. iColoredHadronization needs the event's beam remnants and ISR colour connections, which exist only while the job runs. The bulk can be made in the job or later from stored surfaces.
  • Events without a medium: when the hard collision is the only one, no string is made; Matter showers in vacuum and the bulk unit is empty (has_medium 0).
  • The cores set the rate. An O+O event is small (MUSIC's grid ±10.5 fm), so an O+O job needs ~1.4 GB and ~6 core-s per event; the GPU is far from full.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
The driver is run_prod_oo_isr.py (one job), with the same run_jobs.sh as the Au+Au productions: the same seeds, campaign names, seed registry and restarts (Au+Au jets).

python run_prod_oo_isr.py --events 1 --seed 1 --dry-run      # check the XML/grid, print the plan
python run_prod_oo_isr.py --events 10 --seed 1               # pT-hat 20-40 GeV, b < 3 fm
python run_prod_oo_isr.py --events 30 --seed 1 --pthat-bins 10-20,20-30,30-40 --parton-ymax 0.6
./run_jobs.sh 20 25 0                                        # 20 jobs x 25 events, unique seeds
./run_jobs.sh -j 2 20 25 1 out_had --bulk-hadrons 100 --no-particlize

The image starts in the Au+Au folder, so point it at the O+O one, or call the scripts by their full path (they find their XML and grid next to themselves):

DockerApptainerMac 
OO=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_OO_isr
docker run --rm --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=3 -e OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive -e MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block \
  -v "$HOME/prod:/work" -w "$OO" jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126 \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 8 --mps 32 60 0 /work/OO_a --bulk-hadrons 100 --no-particlize --no-hydro-file

OO=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_OO_isr
apptainer exec --nv --env OMP_NUM_THREADS=3,OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive,MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block \
  --pwd "$OO" --bind "$SCRATCH/prod:/work" xscape_prod.sif \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 8 32 60 0 /work/OO_a --bulk-hadrons 100 --no-particlize --no-hydro-file

cd ~/xscape/examples/prod_OO_isr
python run_prod_oo_isr.py --events 2 --seed 5 --outdir ~/xscape/prod/out_oo
OMP_NUM_THREADS=5 OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive KMP_BLOCKTIME=0 \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 3 --campaign oo_a 20 25 0 ~/xscape/prod/OO_a --bulk-hadrons 100 --no-particlize

That is 32 jobs × 60 events, 8 at a time on one GPU, with all hadrons made in the jobs and nothing else kept. Write the output under the bound /work: the default ./out is inside the read-only image. Nothing needs to be set for iMATTER in the container (the image sets PYTHIA8DATA), and the LBT table cache and --stagger don't apply to these small jobs.

docs.title: Hadronization: in the job or afterwards
docs.text:
setup options files afterwards A. everything in the job --bulk-hadrons 100 --no-particlize <stem>.h5, _hadrons_bulk_bg.h5, _hadrons_jet_frag.h5 nothing to do B. in the job, surfaces kept --bulk-hadrons 100 A + _particlize.h5 more oversamples or other iSS settings any time C. bulk afterwards (the default) none <stem>.h5, _particlize.h5, _hadrons_jet_frag.h5 hadronize.py --tags bulk_bg

Add --no-hydro-file to any of them to leave out the hydro evolution (MUSIC still runs and Matter still reads it). A + --no-hydro-file is a hadrons-only job: the usual production setting, at ~0.13 MB per event with 10 oversamples.

For setup C, the bulk is made on CPUs with the Au+Au production's hadronize.py, always with --tags bulk_bg (the jet hadrons were made in the job; it refuses jet_frag on these files):

python ../prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/hadronize.py out/OO_isr_seed0001_particlize.h5 \
       --tags bulk_bg --oversample 100
python ../prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/run_hadronize.py out -j 4 --tags bulk_bg --oversample 100

In the container, with -w "$OO" (Docker) or --pwd "$OO" (Apptainer) and without --gpus/--nv: ../prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/run_hadronize.py /work/OO_a -j 8 --tags bulk_bg --oversample 100. On SLURM: PROD=oo for utils/slurm_hadronize.sh (Clusters).

The bulk made in the job and afterwards are sampled alike (both use config/hadronize.xml); only the seeds differ. An event at hadron level is unit i of the jet file plus unit i of the bulk file; the bulk's N oversamples share one fluid.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
option default --pthat-min, --pthat-max 20, 40 GeV one pT̂ window --pthat-bins A-B,C-D,… K windows in one job, one Pythia each, event i in window i mod K; no background is shared. Use a multiple of K events --parton-ymax Y, --parton-y-mode {both,any} off, both regenerate the event until the two outgoing partons of the hard scattering have |y| < Y; cross sections corrected by the acceptance --b-min, --b-max 0, 3 fm the impact-parameter range (centrality) --sqrts 200 GeV the collision energy (the parameters are tuned at 200 GeV) --bulk-hadrons N 0 iSS in the job, N oversamples per event --no-particlize, --no-hydro-file, --no-jet-hadrons leave out the particlize file, the hydro file, the jet hadrons --eta-max, --charged, --no-x, --keep-bits-p/-x store less, as for hadronize.py, on both in-job hadron files --keep-primaries N with --bulk-hadrons: also the undecayed bulk hadrons of the first N oversamples, for SMASH later --colour-closure MODE the XML's (reconnect) how iColored closes colour lines that end in the medium: reconnect, reconnect_global, thermal, fake, none --matter-only Matter alone, no LBT and no recoils: a reference for colour studies --store-hadronization-input keep what was handed to Pythia, so rehadronize_jets.py can redo the jet hadrons later --no-subtraction the reference without the hard-momentum subtraction (counts the hard pair's energy twice, on purpose); keep it in its own OUTDIR --late-dtau 0 late step on MUSIC at a constant 0.02 fm/c; keep one setting per campaign --max-skipped N 3 stop the job when more events fail

Choices that change the jets of a seed

X-SCAPE seeds each module from the order it was made. --bulk-hadrons and --no-hydro-file change that order, so the same seed gives other, equally valid jet showers (the hydro is identical). Keep one choice per campaign if jets of different jobs are to be compared event by event.

Before combining files, check the settings every file records (subtraction, b range, late time step, energy loss, colour closure): O+O analysis. Every option and the physics notes: the folder's README.

docs.title: Output and throughput
docs.text:
Each job writes (stem OO_isr_seedNNNN, or OO_isr_<campaign>_NNNN):

file content size per event <stem>_hadrons_jet_frag.h5 the jet hadrons (dijet, ISR emissions, Pythia's MPI partons, the hard pair's remnants), one unit per event, with the whole event record in units/ small <stem>_hadrons_bulk_bg.h5 the bulk, N oversamples per event ~13 kB per oversample <stem>_particlize.h5 MUSIC's freeze-out surface, the final partons, the initiators ~10 MB <stem>.h5 MUSIC's evolution (e, vx, vy, vz) on config/grid_oo.yaml (64 × 64 × 32, x, y ±9.84 fm), with diag/ per event ~17 MB <stem>.xml, .json, .log the job XML, the summary (cross sections, skipped events), the log

A module that throws inside an event costs that event only; the .json lists it under events_skipped.

Measured on 2 × RTX 3090 (24 cores), 8 jobs per GPU with 3 threads, MPS, MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block, 60 events per job:

output events/h per job disk per event hadron files only (--bulk-hadrons 10 --no-particlize --no-hydro-file) 13,728 1.43 GB 0.13 MB full outputs (hydro, particlize, jet hadrons) 12,700 1.40 GB 28 MB

The cores set the rate (~570 events/h per core). Full outputs write ~360 GB/h, more than an OSDF upload takes: use hadron files only, or a large local disk. On two GPUs, utils/launch_2gpu_oo.sh runs one container per GPU with these settings, and on SLURM PROD=oo selects this production in slurm_prod_array.sh: Clusters.
