docs.text:
• O+O analysis: the per-event record, cross-section and N_coll weights, multiplicity, centrality, flow from the oversamples, jets.
  • prod_OO_isr/oo_isr_overview.ipynb: one job's medium and hadrons (needs Jupyter: the analysis venv or the container's xscape-jupyter).
  • Your first event: the same chain from Python with oo_workflow.py.

docs.title: Data on the OSDF
docs.text:
Productions are shared on the OSDF, the Open Science Data Federation of the OSG: a national network of data origins and caches, reached through the Pelican platform. Data sit on an origin under a namespace; clients ask a director for the closest cache and read from it with plain HTTP. For us that means: one place where a production made on a cluster, a workstation or a Mac can go, from which anyone can download it, or read just the part of a file they need without downloading it, from any machine and without an account. js-contrib's namespace is osdf:///fno4hic. Reading it is public; writing needs a login.

What is there

Today the namespace holds example and test productions. In the future, besides the example files, training data sets (for the ML/FNO surrogates) and physics simulation productions will be made available there.

The test data named in this documentation:

path content test/AuAu_0_10_jet_pth10-40_eta06_c1/ the ROOT files of an Au+Au jet campaign (pT̂ 10–40 GeV, 68 files, 2.1 GB), with its campaign file test/h5_read_test/ a small Au+Au hadron file, to try reading in place test/OO_test/ the hadron files of an O+O oo_workflow run, read in place by the notebook pythonic/oo_analysis.ipynb

docs.title: The transfer tool: js_osdf.py
docs.text:
utils/remote_transfer/js_osdf.py lists, downloads, uploads and removes whole productions, single files or patterns, and picks the files by kind. It runs from a js-contrib checkout and makes its own Python environment on its first run (in ~/.cache/js_osdf/venv; a python3 ≥ 3.9 with venv and access to PyPI, a few seconds), so it needs no conda env or venv of yours:

git clone https://github.com/jhputschke/js-contrib.git
cd js-contrib/utils/remote_transfer
./js_osdf.py ls                     # the namespace: one folder per production

Keep it next to transfer_core.py, which it imports. Every command takes remote names as NAME, osdf:///fno4hic/NAME or /fno4hic/NAME.

docs.title: Browsing
docs.text:
./js_osdf.py ls                                  # the top level
./js_osdf.py ls test                             # a folder
./js_osdf.py ls test -r                          # every file below it
./js_osdf.py ls AuAu_c1 --what h5                # a production's files of one kind, with sizes
./js_osdf.py du                                  # space per top-level folder, and the total
./js_osdf.py du AuAu_c1 -d 2 --sort size         # below a folder, two levels, largest first

AuAu_c1 stands for a production folder; ls shows what is there.

docs.title: Downloading
docs.text:
./js_osdf.py download AuAu_c1 --what h5 --to /scratch            # -> /scratch/AuAu_c1/
./js_osdf.py download AuAu_c1 --what root --to /scratch          # only the ROOT files
./js_osdf.py download 'AuAu_c1/*_000[1-5]_*' --to /scratch/few   # a pattern (quoted): a few jobs
./js_osdf.py download AuAu_c1 --what h5 --to /scratch --dry-run  # what would come, and how much

The kinds go by file name:

--what files for h5 <stem>_particlize.h5, <stem>_hadrons_*.h5, the hadronization logs the hadron analyses: HadronFileReader needs the particlize files next to the hadron files, and h5 brings them along root <stem>_hadrons.root, <campaign>_campaign.root ROOT analyses alone: complete on their own pair <stem>.h5, the hydro (~0.17–0.29 GB per event), with its .json, .xml, .log the hydro, the wake observables, FNO training all (default) everything in the folder
  • Resumable and checked. Files already there with the same size and CRC32C are skipped, so an interrupted download finishes when the command runs again. Each file is written as <file>.part and renamed only when its size and checksum are right.
  • Where they go: a folder to --to/<folder>/, files and patterns to --to/<file>.
  • -j N transfers N files at once (default 4). Measured: ~69 MB/s down from a workstation.
  • --what takes a comma list (h5,root).

docs.title: Reading files in place
docs.text:
In the analysis environment (pelicanfs is installed by default) and in the production container, osdf:// paths can be read without downloading: pelicanfs finds a cache for the path and reads by byte ranges, so only the parts asked for travel. Both examples read public test files and run as they are:

import uproot
c = uproot.open("osdf:///fno4hic/test/AuAu_0_10_jet_pth10-40_eta06_c1/pth10-40_eta06_c1_campaign.root")
sigma = c["windows"].arrays(["sigma_mb"], library="np")["sigma_mb"]   # the pT-hat windows' cross sections

import fsspec, h5py, hdf5plugin                   # hdf5plugin: the Blosc filter of the HDF5 files
fs = fsspec.filesystem("osdf")
with fs.open("/fno4hic/test/h5_read_test/AuAu_0_10_jet_st1_t000_0001_hadrons_bulk_jet.h5", "rb",
             cache_type="blockcache", block_size=2**20) as fo, h5py.File(fo, "r") as f:
    so = f["hadrons/sample_offsets"][:]
    p = f["hadrons/p"][so[3]:so[4]]               # one oversample's momenta (E, px, py, pz)
  • Pass cache_type="blockcache", block_size=2**20 for HDF5: fsspec's default read-ahead re-fetches overlapping ranges when HDF5 jumps back to its metadata. With 1 MB blocks, one oversample of a 100 MB hadron file moved 6.3 MB instead of 31.5 MB.
  • Time: the first open in a process takes ~1–1.5 s (pelicanfs finds a cache); after that, one oversample ~0.1–0.2 s.
  • When to download instead: for whole productions and for anything read more than once (in place, every pass goes over the network again). HadronFileReader, ParticlizeFile, run_h5toROOT.py and the analysis/ scripts take local paths only.
  • Inside the production container the pelican command line does the same for single files: pelican object get osdf:///fno4hic/… /work/….

What the files hold and how to read them: What a production writes, Hadrons, ROOT and C++.

docs.title: Uploading
docs.text:
Writing to /fno4hic needs write access to the namespace: a browser login, or a bearer token. Whatever is uploaded can be read by everyone.

./js_osdf.py login              # once: prints a link; log in and approve in any browser
./js_osdf.py status             # who, the scopes, the time left of the token and the login
./js_osdf.py upload /data/AuAu_c1 --what h5 --dry-run       # what would go
./js_osdf.py upload /data/AuAu_c1 --what h5                 # -> osdf:///fno4hic/AuAu_c1/
./js_osdf.py upload /data/out --what root --as AuAu_pth10-40_v1   # another folder name
./js_osdf.py rm -r AuAu_c1 --dry-run                         # what would be removed
  • The login lasts 15 days (renewals don't extend it): log in again before a long run would pass that date. It is kept in ~/.config/js_osdf/web/ and used by every later command. logout revokes it. A bearer token works too (--token-file, $BEARER_TOKEN_FILE, …).
  • Uploads of a directory go to osdf:///fno4hic/[PREFIX/]<directory name>/ (--as NAME for another name, --prefix for a parent folder). Only the files directly in the directory are sent, not its subdirectories: upload gpu0/, gpu1/ or t000/, … one by one (with --as CAMPAIGN/gpu0) or use upload_follow.py below.
  • Unfinished files are left out: HDF5 files whose complete attribute is false (a job still writing) and *.part files.
  • Checked: Pelican reports sizes but no checksums, so after each upload js_osdf.py checks the size at the origin and records size and CRC32C in a manifest in the remote folder; downloads are checked against it. Don't run two uploads into the same folder at once.
  • rm asks first (--yes doesn't; --dry-run lists all). Removed files can't be brought back.

Measured: ~80 MB/s up from a workstation, 4 or 8 files at once alike.

docs.title: Uploading while a production runs
docs.text:
A campaign can write faster than a local disk holds. utils/upload_follow.py uploads each job as soon as its <stem>.json says complete and, if asked, deletes the local copies after a verified upload, so the local disk no longer limits the campaign:

utils/upload_follow.py /data/AuAu_a AuAu_a                      # one pass, upload only
utils/upload_follow.py /data/AuAu_a AuAu_a --follow --delete pair   # while the campaign runs
touch /data/AuAu_a/.upload_final       # when the campaign is done: a last pass, then it exits
option --delete none (default) / pair / all after a verified upload, delete nothing / <stem>.h5 (the hydro) / also <stem>_particlize.h5 --keep-free SIZE with pair/all: delete only while the disk has less than SIZE free, the oldest uploads first --verify-every N before deleting, download every Nth file and compare it byte by byte (default 20; 0: never) --follow repeat every --interval s (default 60) until OUTBASE/.upload_final appears or --follow-pid ends
  • Verified means: the origin holds a file of the local size, the manifest's CRC32C matches the local file, and every Nth file was downloaded and compared. The .json, .log and .xml files are never deleted (run_jobs.sh needs the .json to skip finished jobs).
  • It runs on the host, next to Docker or on a node that sees a SLURM campaign's directories, from a js-contrib checkout; any directory of run_jobs.sh output directories works (OUTBASE/<sub>/ → REMOTE/<sub>/). Its state survives restarts (OUTBASE/upload_state.json, log in OUTBASE/upload.log).
  • With launch_2gpu.sh, --upload REMOTE --delete pair starts it with the campaign (Clusters). launch_2gpu.sh --upload refuses to start without a login.
  • Hadronization output is uploaded afterwards: js_osdf.py upload OUTBASE/gpu0 --as REMOTE/gpu0 --what h5,root.

What to move where. The particlize files are self-contained (surfaces, partons, shower initiators), so hadronization on another cluster and the analysis need only --what h5; the large pair files (--what pair) only go where the hydro is used, e.g. FNO training.

docs.title: Google Cloud Storage
docs.text:
js_gcs.py, next to js_osdf.py, has the same commands and options for a Google Cloud Storage bucket (default gs://test_fno). The bucket is not public: reading and writing need a service-account JSON key (--key-file, $JS_GCS_KEY_FILE or $GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS). The analysis environment reads gs:// paths with --with-gcs.

./js_gcs.py upload /data/AuAu_a --what pair -j 8     # -> gs://test_fno/AuAu_a/
./js_gcs.py download AuAu_a --what root --to /scratch

All options, credentials and the tests: utils/remote_transfer/README.md.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Analysis environment: the venv that reads these files, with pelicanfs.
  • Notebooks: oo_analysis.ipynb streams the O+O test files from the OSDF.

docs.title: Z+jet and other collision systems
docs.text: The physics of a production is in its user XML, so a new collision system or a different hard process is mostly a copy of an XML with a few lines changed. This page covers the two cases that already exist: the Z+jet production in Pb+Pb at 5.02 TeV, made for the CMS and ATLAS Z–hadron and Z+jet measurements, and Pb+Pb jets at the LHC from your own XML, with the steps to take for any other system. Both run through the Au+Au jet production's driver run_prod_jet.py, so everything in Au+Au jets applies. At the end, the production wizard plans the launch command for any of the productions.

docs.title: Z+jet in Pb+Pb at 5.02 TeV
docs.text:
The Z+jet production runs Pb+Pb collisions at √s_NN = 5.02 TeV, 0–30 %, with a hard process that makes a Z boson decaying to e⁺e⁻ or μ⁺μ⁻ and a recoiling parton. The Z's leptons pass through the medium untouched, so the Z tags the initial jet momentum; the recoil jet loses energy and leaves a wake. The inputs are in example/config/ (in the image: /opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/config):

  • PbPb_0_30_ZJet.xml: the Pb+Pb jet XML at 0–30 % (b_max 8.57 fm) with a Z+jet <PythiaGun> (Z + parton processes, Z → ee/μμ, <trigger>Z);
  • grid_PbPb.yaml: the larger Pb+Pb output grid (80 × 80 × 40 cells, x, y ±15.3 fm), for the edge flags;
  • hadronize.xml: the shared hadronization settings; its eCMforHadronization is set to the collision's 5020 GeV from the XML's PythiaGun automatically.

docs.title: The settings
docs.text:
The campaigns use six pT̂ windows with 4 jets per window per background (24 events per background), the Z's leptons inside the detector acceptance, and hadron files made in the job:

option --user-xml …/PbPb_0_30_ZJet.xml --grid …/grid_PbPb.yaml the Z+jet XML and the Pb+Pb grid --pthat-bins 20-30,30-35,35-45,45-55,55-70,70-200 --jets-per-bin 4 the windows: the p_T^Z > 40 GeV cross section is spread evenly over them, so little is lost to the window weights --lepton-ptmin 20 --lepton-etamax 2.5 both leptons p_T > 20 GeV, |η| < 2.5 (the CMS and ATLAS Z–hadron cuts); failing events are regenerated before any hydro, and the cross sections corrected --hadrons-only --oversample 40 --n-frag 40 --correlated hadron files only, 40 correlated samples per jet event --eta-max 2.6 --no-x --hadron-keep-bits-p 12 --hadron-keep-bits-x 8 --keep-primaries 0 all final particles at |η| < 2.6, no positions, rounded TAG_PREFIX=PbPb_0_30_seed (environment) names the files PbPb_0_30_<campaign>_… instead of AuAu_0_10_jet_…

--trigger Z comes from the XML; --trigger-ymax Y would add a Z rapidity cut (the campaigns apply |y_Z| offline). There is no cut on the recoiling parton.

A current image

The Z trigger, --hadrons-only and TAG_PREFIX need an image built from the current code. Check it first: python run_prod_jet.py --help must list --trigger, and a --dry-run must print trigger Z (lepton pT > 20 GeV, lepton |eta| < 2.5), EOS 91 and eCMforHadronization 5020. Pin the image by digest for the campaign.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
Check with --dry-run inside the image (no GPU work), then run. In Docker:

IMG=jhputschke/xscape-prod:cu126                      # pinned by digest for a campaign
D=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/config
mkdir -p ~/prod/lbt_cache
docker run -d --name zjet --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e TAG_PREFIX=PbPb_0_30_seed -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=5 -e OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive \
  -e MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block -e LBT_TABLE_CACHE=/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin \
  -v "$HOME/prod:/work" $IMG \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 3 --stagger 12 --campaign zjet_test 10 96 0 /work/zjet_test \
    --user-xml $D/PbPb_0_30_ZJet.xml --grid $D/grid_PbPb.yaml \
    --pthat-bins 20-30,30-35,35-45,45-55,55-70,70-200 --jets-per-bin 4 \
    --lepton-ptmin 20 --lepton-etamax 2.5 \
    --hadrons-only --oversample 40 --n-frag 40 --correlated \
    --eta-max 2.6 --no-x --hadron-keep-bits-p 12 --hadron-keep-bits-x 8 --keep-primaries 0

Ten jobs of 96 events (4 backgrounds each), three at a time: a Pb+Pb Z+jet job peaks at 14–16 GB of host memory (2.1× an Au+Au job; measured on the GB10), mostly MUSIC's larger box. It takes 2.1× the time of an Au+Au jet job and writes 1.7× the disk.

The scripts of the published campaigns are in utils/zjet/: ten campaigns zjet_c00 … zjet_c09 of 9,600 events each (100 jobs × 96 events), with disjoint seed ranges (campaign C uses seeds from 1 + 1000 C), so campaigns from different machines combine. Run them from a js-contrib checkout:

script runs zjet_slurm_campaign.sh one campaign as a SLURM array through utils/slurm_prod_array.sh: C=0 sbatch zjet_slurm_campaign.sh (set up for NCSA Delta's A40 nodes, 3 jobs per GPU; edit the #SBATCH lines for your site). C=0 NJOBS=1 is a ~1,000-event smoke test zjet_3090_campaign.sh one campaign on a two-GPU workstation through utils/launch_2gpu.sh: IMAGE=… ./zjet_3090_campaign.sh 0 zjet_3090_test.sh before the first campaign on a workstation: info (digest, commits, dry run), bench 3, bench 4, report, smoke

After each campaign: utils/check_deposition.py OUTDIR (Clusters), then the upload to the OSDF (Data on the OSDF).

docs.title: The pp reference
docs.text:
prod_AuAu_0_10_jet/run_prod_vacuum.py runs the same XML's PythiaGun and Matter in vacuum (no initial state, hydro, LBT or liquefier), with Colorless hadronization at the PythiaGun's energy. It runs on the CPU, ~0.02 s per event on the GB10, so 12,000 events take minutes:

python run_prod_vacuum.py --events 12000 --seed 900001 --campaign zjet_pp \
  --user-xml $D/PbPb_0_30_ZJet.xml --pthat-bins 20-30,30-35,35-45,45-55,55-70,70-200 \
  --lepton-ptmin 20 --lepton-etamax 2.5 \
  --n-frag 40 --eta-max 2.6 --no-x --hadron-keep-bits-p 12 --outdir /work/zjet_pp

It writes one <stem>_hadrons_jet_frag.h5 (attribute vacuum), read like the Pb+Pb jet files. Give it seeds of its own: the Pb+Pb campaigns' seeds would give the same Pythia events.

docs.title: What to know in the files
docs.text:
• The Z per event is in units/ of the hadron files (z_pt, z_y, z_phi, z_m, lep{1,2}_{pid,pt,eta,phi}); every paper's p_T^Z and mass window is applied offline.
  • Weight every event by its n_coll (units/n_coll): the geometry is drawn with P(b) ∝ b over 0–30 % and every event has one Z, while Z production scales with N_coll. Weight also by the window's cross section.
  • The two leptons are among the jet hadrons (jet_frag, pid ±11/±13) and in initiators/: remove them before a track or jet analysis.
  • Every background has its event plane near φ = 0 (3dMCGlauber puts the impact parameter along x). The means of a Z-frame analysis are unaffected; event mixing needs each background rotated by a random angle, which the Z-analysis scripts do by default.

The Z–hadron and Z+jet analyses, step by step: analysis/zjet/ and Hadrons. The campaign design (windows, cuts, expected statistics): utils/zjet/README.md.

docs.title: Another collision system: Pb+Pb at the LHC
docs.text: run_prod_jet.py takes a copy of AuAu_MCGlauber_MUSIC_0_10_jet.xml with --user-xml, fills in the job and checks it. So another system or energy is a copy of the XML with the collision changed. Here: Pb+Pb at √s_NN = 5.02 TeV, 0–10 %; the same steps apply to other nuclei and energies.

docs.title: 1. The XML
docs.text:
where Au+Au 200 GeV Pb+Pb 5.02 TeV why <IS><MCGlauber><projectile>, <target> Au Pb <IS><MCGlauber><sqrts> 200 5020 <IS><MCGlauber><b_max> 4.7 fm 4.95 fm centrality comes from b inside X-SCAPE (cenMin/cenMax are ignored): the geometric 0–10 %, π b² = 0.1 × 7.7 b <IS><grid_max_x>, <grid_max_y> 15 20 MUSIC's grid: the fireball is larger and lives longer <IS><grid_max_z> 6 8 MUSIC's η_s range: the beam rapidity is 8.5 instead of 5.4 <Hard><PythiaGun><eCM> 200 5020 the pT̂ windows 10–40 GeV your choice --pthat-bins

eCMforHadronization follows the collision automatically, so the one hadronize.xml serves every system. From a js-contrib checkout:

mkdir -p xml
T=contribs/PyJetscape/example/config
sed -e 's#<projectile>Au</projectile>#<projectile>Pb</projectile>#' \
    -e 's#<target>Au</target>#<target>Pb</target>#' \
    -e 's#<sqrts>200</sqrts>#<sqrts>5020</sqrts>#' \
    -e 's#<b_max>4.7</b_max>#<b_max>4.95</b_max>#' \
    -e 's#<grid_max_x> 15 </grid_max_x>#<grid_max_x> 20 </grid_max_x>#' \
    -e 's#<grid_max_y> 15 </grid_max_y>#<grid_max_y> 20 </grid_max_y>#' \
    -e 's#<grid_max_z> 6  </grid_max_z>#<grid_max_z> 8  </grid_max_z>#' \
    -e 's#<eCM>200</eCM>#<eCM>5020</eCM>#' \
    $T/AuAu_MCGlauber_MUSIC_0_10_jet.xml > xml/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml
diff $T/AuAu_MCGlauber_MUSIC_0_10_jet.xml xml/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml     # 8 lines must differ

The result is already in example/config/ as PbPb_0_10_jet.xml, with grid_PbPb.yaml; use them as they are or as a start for another system.

What the driver checks (it refuses an XML that breaks the two-stage setup, before any event): exactly two <Hydro><MUSIC> blocks, MUSIC_1 (background) and MUSIC_2 (jet leg), all MUSIC settings in the first; the liquefier's <dtau> equal to MUSIC's starting step; a <Hard><PythiaGun> block; no <SoftParticlization>, <JetHadronization>, <Afterburner> or writers (the hadrons come from stage 2); an output grid inside MUSIC's grid.

Choices to make before a production:

  • The tune. The 3D MC-Glauber, viscosity, freeze-out and energy-loss parameters are those of the Au+Au 200 GeV production; none is tuned at the LHC. Check the bulk against data first (ALICE: dN_ch/dη at |η| < 0.5 is 1943 ± 54 at 0–5 % and 1587 ± 47 at 5–10 %).
  • Pythia's MPI. PythiaGun switches multi-parton interactions on, and every parton it hands over is showered and can deposit; at 5.02 TeV that is many more partons than at 200 GeV. PartonLevel:MPI = off in <LinesToRead> leaves the hard process and its ISR.
  • The output grid. The default grid (±12.2 fm) fits, but the jet leg can reach its edge: grid_PbPb.yaml is larger with the same cells (files of different grids don't go into one training set).
  • Names. TAG_PREFIX=PbPb_0_10_seed names the files PbPb_0_10_… (letters, digits, ., _, -, ending in _seed; one per OUTDIR), or put the system into the campaign name.

docs.title: 2. Your XML from outside the container
docs.text:
The XML doesn't need to be in the image. Bind its directory and give the driver the path as the container sees it, as an absolute path:

bind then Docker -v "$PWD/xml:/xml:ro" --user-xml /xml/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml Apptainer --bind "$PWD/xml:/xml", or nothing for a file under $HOME --user-xml /xml/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml SLURM (slurm_prod_array.sh, slurm_hadronize.sh) BINDS="$PWD/xml:/xml" in EXTRA_ARGS (stage 1) or HAD_ARGS (stage 2)

The same holds for --grid, --main-xml and --hadronize-xml. The file is read when a job starts, and each job stores the XML it ran (<stem>.xml, prod_user_xml): don't edit it during a campaign.

docs.title: 3. A first event, then the campaign
docs.text:
# in the container (Apptainer; Docker with -v "$PWD/xml:/xml:ro" -v "$PWD/prod:/work")
PROD=/opt/X-SCAPE/external_packages/js-contrib/contribs/PyJetscape/example/prod_AuAu_0_10_jet
apptainer exec --nv --env MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block --pwd "$PROD" \
  --bind "$PWD/xml:/xml,$SCRATCH/prod:/work" xscape_prod.sif \
  python run_prod_jet.py --user-xml /xml/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml --events 3 --seed 1 \
    --write-particlize both --outdir /work/PbPb_test --out PbPb_0_10_jet_seed0001.h5 --dry-run
# ... the same without --dry-run, then stage 2
apptainer exec --pwd "$PROD" --bind "$PWD/xml:/xml,$SCRATCH/prod:/work" xscape_prod.sif \
  ./run_hadronize.py /work/PbPb_test -j 3 --oversample 100 --n-frag 20

One event against Au+Au, measured on the GB10 (one job alone, pT̂ 50–70 GeV, --write-particlize both, default output grid, 100 oversamples):

Pb+Pb 5.02 TeV Au+Au 200 GeV wall time of the event (both legs) 38.9 s 17.1 s peak host memory of the job 15.7 GB 6.1 GB freeze-out cells per leg 2.55 M 1.0 M showers, droplets, deposited energy 18, 74, 336 GeV 2, 25, 32 GeV pair file, particlize file 321 MB, 395 MB 245 MB, 155 MB hadron file per leg (100 oversamples) 79 MB 19 MB dN_ch/dη, |η| < 0.5, background 1534 ± 4 (ALICE 0–10 %: ~1765) 577 ± 2

The campaign is the Au+Au one with the XML (and the grid) passed after OUTDIR:

DockerSLURM 
docker run -d --gpus all --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=3 -e OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive -e MUSIC_CUDA_SYNC=block \
  -e LBT_TABLE_CACHE=/work/lbt_cache/lbt_tables_v1.bin \
  -v "$PWD/xml:/xml:ro" -v "$HOME/prod:/work" $IMG \
  ./run_jobs.sh -j 4 --stagger 12 --campaign PbPb_c1 20 15 0 /work/PbPb_c1 \
    --user-xml /xml/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml --grid /xml/grid_PbPb.yaml \
    --pthat-bins 40-60,60-80,80-100 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both

# stage 1: ~16 GB per job, so fewer jobs per GPU than for Au+Au
SIF=$PWD/xscape_prod.sif CAMPAIGN=PbPb_c1 P=5 BINDS="$PWD/xml:/xml" \
  EXTRA_ARGS="--user-xml /xml/PbPb_0_10_jet.xml --grid /xml/grid_PbPb.yaml --pthat-bins 40-60,60-80,80-100 --jets-per-bin 5 --parton-ymax 0.6 --write-particlize both" \
  sbatch --array=0-19 --cpus-per-task=20 --mem=96G utils/slurm_prod_array.sh
# stage 2
SIF=$PWD/xscape_prod.sif CAMPAIGN=PbPb_c1 \
  HAD_ARGS="--oversample 200 --n-frag 50 --keep-bits-p 12 --keep-bits-x 8" \
  sbatch --array=0-19 --mem=48G utils/slurm_hadronize.sh
  • Memory: plan ~16 GB per job, 4–5 jobs on 96 GB; measure events/h with a short sweep of P on the first node.
  • Disk: ~0.7 GB per event with a new background every event; a background shared by 15 jets saves most of the background's share. Hadrons are ~4× Au+Au per oversample, so 200 oversamples give the statistics of 400–500 in Au+Au.
  • Stage 2 memory: ~2.3 GB per process at 100 oversamples.
  • Hydro-only Pb+Pb (prod_AuAu_0_10/run_prod.py) takes the same <IS> changes in a copy of its XML.

Here the grid is bound from xml/: copy grid_PbPb.yaml there, or pass the image's own path. Full details: docs/README_2stage.md, §9.

docs.title: Planning a production: the wizard
docs.text:
utils/prodwizard.py plans a campaign before anything runs. Pick a production preset and a machine; it writes the launch command with the settings measured for that machine (launch_2gpu.sh on a two-GPU workstation, run_jobs.sh on a single machine or Mac, slurm_prod_array.sh on a cluster) and estimates events/h, duration, disk and memory, each marked as measured or estimated with its source. It checks the plan: events per job a multiple of the pT̂ windows × jets, memory, disk, upload rate, the image, the campaign name. It never starts jobs.

utils/prodwizard.py --list                 # presets and machines
utils/prodwizard.py --preset auau_jet --machine 2x3090 --events 2700 --campaign c5 --out /data/c5
utils/prodwizard.py --preset pbpb_zjet --machine slurm_a40 --events 19200 --gpus 20 \
    --campaign zjet_c10 --save launch_zjet_c10.sh      # a script, the plan in its header
utils/prodwizard.py                        # the interactive wizard: a form, the plan beside it
presets (--preset) auau_jet Au+Au jets, pair + particlize files (the campaign setting) auau_particlize_only Au+Au jets, particlize file only auau_hadrons_only Au+Au jets, hadron files only, in the job oo_hadrons, oo_full O+O with ISR: hadron files only; or the default outputs pbpb_zjet Pb+Pb 5.02 TeV 0–30 % Z+jet, hadron files only

The machines (--machine) are 2x3090, gb10, m3max and SLURM nodes with one slurm_v100, slurm_a40, slurm_a100 or slurm_l40s per array task; further options set --events-per-job, --image, --first-seed, --jobs-per-gpu, --omp, --upload, --delete and --min-free. The command-line mode needs only the standard library; the interactive wizard needs textual (in the analysis venv), and runs in a browser with textual serve "utils/prodwizard.py". The presets and measured rates are in utils/prod_presets.json.
